findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext long-lived static credentials. EC2 user data is readable via the instance metadata service by anyone with code execution or SSRF on the host, and is also visible to any principal with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute.

The instance is launched into a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true whose route table has a default route to an internet gateway, and is guarded by a security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on ports 22 and 80. The host carrying plaintext AWS credentials is therefore directly reachable from the internet.

No metadata_options block is configured, so IMDSv1 with optional tokens remains available. Combined with an internet-facing web server and secrets stored in user data, a single SSRF flaw allows retrieval of the user data and any instance role credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the instance root volume is created without enforced EBS encryption at rest (unless account-level default encryption happens to be on).
Ingress permits TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration of a publicly addressed instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and remote exploitation.

Egress allows all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting unrestricted exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised host, and ingress on port 80 serves cleartext HTTP from the internet with no TLS listener configured anywhere.
The EBS volume is created with the encrypted attribute explicitly commented out, so data written to the volume attached to the web host is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted volume and no encryption is configured, so snapshot data is stored in plaintext and can be copied or shared without any key-based access control.

The VPC flow log destination bucket declares no server-side encryption configuration, so network telemetry that can reveal internal addressing and traffic patterns is stored without enforced encryption.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block and TLS policy
findings.description: No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL restriction, or bucket policy requiring aws:SecureTransport is defined for the log bucket, leaving no defence-in-depth against accidental public exposure or cleartext retrieval of flow logs.

force_destroy = true with no versioning or object lock means the flow-log bucket and its contents can be deleted or overwritten in a single operation, allowing an attacker with write access to destroy security evidence.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance placed in this subnet automatically receives a public IP, and the associated route table routes 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway, removing the network boundary for all workloads in the subnet.
